subject: Capacity true-up & surge handoff — Adeptly Therapeutics renewal
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@adeptly.com>
Cc: Carlos Torres <c.torres@procure-adeptly.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal capacity true-up & initial proposal

Hi Priya —

As we approach your Nov renewal, I pulled a utilization slice from Q3 and the first half of Q4 to baseline Adeptly's steady-state GPU consumption. I attached the export (adeptly-usage-export-2027Q3.csv) and a high-level proposal PDF with two options. High level:

- Observed 7d rolling utilization averages show a persistent 65–72% GPU utilization during peak business hours across the 00:00–06:00 UTC window (model mix: chat + embeddings + rerank).
- We recommend a repack that shifts 12 GPUs from hot-standby into committed capacity and adds 8 GPUs to the burst pool to handle episodic spikes (holiday tests + simulated load).

As an ask: can you share if procurement needs a standard PO vs DocuSign? Also curious if you want the renewal to include an SLA uplift (we can quote 99.9% latency SLA for committed pools).

Proposed next step: 30m call this week, I can walk through the usage graphs and two billing options. If you'd prefer, I can send a redlined SOW for Option B (lower commit + burst credit) for quick approval.

Thanks —
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

From: Priya Singh <priya@adeptly.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal capacity true-up & initial proposal

Hi Connor —

Thanks for the quick analysis and the attachments — very helpful. A few clarifying q's before we sync:

1) Can you provide the delta in monthly run-rate cost between the two options (commit 40 GPUs vs commit 28 + burst)? Prefer line items (GPU hrs, burst credits, observability add-on).
2) If we do the repack (move 12 GPUs out of hot-standby into committed), how long to execute with minimal disruption? We need <2 hour maintenance windows for our traffic.
3) On the SLA uplift: what is the effective SLA for model fallbacks if a committed pool is at capacity?

Procurement (cc'd) prefers a PO; they'll include payment terms in the PO and we use DocuSign for signature only on the SOW.

Can do a 30m call Thursday 10:00 PT if that works.

— Priya
Priya Singh
Head of ML Platforms, Adeptly Therapeutics
priay.singh@adeptly.com | +1 617 555 2424

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal capacity true-up & initial proposal

Team — forwarding Priya's questions; summarized asks below. Quick alignment before Thursday's call:

> Priya Q1: cost delta (A: 40 commit vs B: 28 commit + burst)
> Priya Q2: execution window for repack (<2 hours required)
> Priya Q3: SLA + fallback behavior when committed pool saturates

Ben — can you confirm the migration playbook timing (repack live with rolling instance swaps)? We had previously quoted a 90–120 minute window but that assumed a cold network. If we use the repack + staged prefix caching, we might be able to do 45–60 minutes.

Kimberly — pricing sensitivity: Priya said procurement wants PO (no upfront Card). Can we present both pricing tables and call out the effective monthly run-rate difference? I recommend we make Option B the recommended path (lower committed spend, burst credits for load tests) but highlight the slightly higher per-token charge on burst.

Marissa — after call we'll need an operational checklist for the repack: pre-checks, traffic shadowing, KV cache pre-warm, rollback steps, and a one-hour maintenance window ask. Can you own that?

If we agree, I'll send a revised SOW for Option B with a cost comparison attachment and the DocuSign link.

— Connor

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@adeptly.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Carlos Torres <c.torres@procure-adeptly.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal options & proposed next steps (Option A / Option B)

Hi Priya & Carlos —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion I attached a redlined SOW for Option B (redline-sow-optionB.pdf) and a cost-comparison sheet (cost-comparison-sheet.xlsx). TL;DR:

- Option A (Recommended for scale & predictability): 40 committed GPUs, includes 99.9% latency SLA on committed pool, dedicated hot-standby (6 GPUs) for failover. Estimated monthly run-rate: $182,400.
- Option B (Lower commit, more flexible): 28 committed GPUs + 20,000 burst credits/month (approx equivalent to 12 GPUs of episodic usage). No SLA uplift by default; we can add SLA for an incremental fee. Estimated monthly run-rate: $141,200 (base) + burst consumption overage.

Operational notes:
- Repack timing: Ben confirmed a phased repack that leverages prefix/KV cache warmup, targeted draining of standby nodes and slot reassignment. We estimate a 45–75 minute maintenance window with a 2-stage rollback tested on staging beforehand.
- Fallback behavior: when committed pool is saturated, requests route to burst pool variants with slightly higher latency and best-effort throttling; critical paths can be pinned to reserved model variants if required.

Next steps:
1) If you prefer Option B, send the PO referencing 'SOW-RI-ADEPTLY-2027-11 Option B' and we'll route the DocuSign for countersign. Link below sends the draft to your procurement.
2) Marissa will share the pre-deploy checklist and schedule a 2-hour maintenance window in staging for the repack rehearsal.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/track/ABC-adeptly-optionB
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12456-DEAL-2027-089

Thanks, and happy to jump on another call if you want an internal walkthrough of the repack steps.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-sow-optionB.pdf (PDF, 220KB), cost-comparison-sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)
